import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Primitive roots of the form k² + 1

Every prime $p$ has a primitive root $0 < g < p$ of the form $k^2 + 1$, where $k$ is an integer.

Zhi-Wei Sun has offered a prize of RMB 2,000 for the first proof.

*References:*
- [A239957](https://oeis.org/A239957)
- Z.-W. Sun, "New observations on primitive roots modulo primes," arXiv:1405.0290 [math.NT], 2014.
-/

namespace OeisA239957

/-- The predicate that $p$ has a primitive root $0 < g < p$ of the form $k^2 + 1$, where $k$ is an integer. -/
def A (p : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∃ k : ℤ, k ^ 2 + 1 < p ∧ orderOf (k ^ 2 + 1 : ZMod p) = p - 1

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_2 : A 2 :=
  ⟨0, by norm_num, by norm_num⟩

/--
**Zhi-Wei Sun's Conjecture (A239957)**: Every prime $p$ has a primitive root $0 < g < p$ of the
form $k^2 + 1$, where $k$ is an integer.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem conjecture (p : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime) : A p := by
  sorry

end OeisA239957

reformulations.difference: The definition substitutes k² + 1 directly for g, omits an explicit positivity condition, and expresses primitivity using orderOf in ZMod p rather than a generator of its unit group.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For every integer k, k² + 1 > 0, and the integer-to-ZMod cast preserves this polynomial. For prime p, p - 1 > 0; an element of order p - 1 is therefore a unit. Its order is unchanged upon viewing it in the unit group, whose cardinality is p - 1, so the order condition is equivalent to generating that group. The converse follows identically. Proved this pointwise equivalence for every prime p as ReviewA239957.A_iff_source in /workspace/review/scratch.lean, without using the conjecture.

sources_consulted: OEIS A239957, including comments (i)–(ii), examples, and programs, read through the official data mirror: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/oeis/oeisdata/main/seq/A239/A239957.seq
Z.-W. Sun, "New observations on primitive roots modulo primes," arXiv:1405.0290v5, Introduction, Conjecture 3.1 and Remark 3.1; TeX source: https://arxiv.org/e-print/1405.0290v5
review.notes: Checked all three declarations. The conjecture faithfully states OEIS comment (i), also Conjecture 3.1(i) in Sun's paper; both consulted sources still record it as a conjecture. The proved test a_2 correctly uses k = 0 and g = 1. Scratch checks exclude A 0 and A 1, verify several small-prime cases, and rule out zero-residue/default-order witnesses at prime moduli. Computed counts agree with all 80 listed OEIS terms. Direct OEIS web views were blocked by Cloudflare, so its official data mirror was used. No edits were made to the reviewed file.
